crime_highlights: he fled in the vehicle, nearly hitting the police constable
He drove through a stop sign and broadsided another vehicle
The occupants of the vehicle that was hit were seriously injured
The female occupant was unconscious, with a broken ankle, sternum, wrist, pelvis and neck
rationale_highlights: He discussed Mr. Bailey's experience of family dysfunction (including intergenerational effects of residential schools)
The judge was required to consider the appellant's antecedents, including his Aboriginal background in assessing moral culpability
treated them as factors justifying a more lenient sentence than otherwise would have been imposed

crime_highlights: Mr. Biwer approached the Ford Escape and pushed Monica Johanson in the chest
Mr. Biwer ignored her, entered the vehicle and drove away with the child still inside
The accused had abandoned the vehicle and the child
rationale_highlights: Mr. Biwer has been affected by a multi-generational familial history of substance abuse, instability, violence, criminality and premature death
The sentencing judge must evaluate the effect of the aboriginal offender's background in fashioning the ultimate sentence imposed
concluded that Mr. Biwer's aboriginal background justified a sentence of 10 years rather than 11 years that might otherwise have been imposed
note: Crime para 5-6 includes some embedded background; para 4 too long.
